newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt approves Leciva MBO - paper.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt approves Leciva MBO - paper.

text.p: The Czech government has approved the sale of a 66 percent of pharmaceutical maker Leciva a.s. to management, according to a report in the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes on Thursday.
"A final contract has not been closed, and because of this, I would not like to disclose the price," the paper quoted Leciva Director Jiri Michal as saying.

The paper, without attribution, said the offer by Leciva was around two billion crowns. Leciva shares were trading at about 2,360 crowns last week when the approval was made, putting the stake's value at some 2.3 billion crowns.
Government and Leciva officials were not immediately available for comment on the report.

The paper quoted Martin Kocourek, an economic adviser to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, as saying Leciva management had shown it was very capable of running the company and the sale of the stake to a foreign investor could have been harmful.

"It's possible that foreign investors may have paid more. (But) there were great concerns that a foreign owner would have used Leciva's position on the market to offer its own drugs, which tend to be about 10 percent more expensive," Kocourek said.
